evals.prompt: Northwind Legal wants our vendor onboarding policy as a Word doc so they can track changes. It's in docs/vendor-onboarding.md: a # title, ## sections, a numbered approval process with sub-steps, a pipe table of approval limits ($5,000 / $50,000 / unlimited), a footnote citing the finance policy, and a Mermaid flowchart of the approval path. Use ./brand/brand.json and A4 paper.
assertions: Runs md_to_docx.py with --brand ./brand/brand.json and --page a4, writing a .docx
Deals with the Mermaid flowchart before converting: renders it to PNG with mermaid-render and embeds it, or says plainly that it stays as code
Moves the footnote's text into the body or a Notes section instead of letting it drop silently
Reports every WARN line the script printed, each with what was done about it
Keeps the approval limits ($5,000 / $50,000 / unlimited) and every other fact exactly as in the source
Checks the file opens (textutil, Quick Look, LibreOffice or Word) and reports the script's summary counts
Tells the user the headings drive Word's navigation pane and table of contents

evals.prompt: Convert this to Word for the Acme client, they don't use Markdown: <a 40-line Markdown status report pasted in the chat, with **Background** and **Next steps** as bold lines instead of headings, an HTML <table>, and an image linked from https://cdn.example.com/chart.png>
assertions: Saves the pasted text to a .md file before converting
Turns the bold-line pseudo-headings into ## headings so Word sees them as headings
Rewrites the HTML table as a pipe table rather than letting it drop
Says the remote image is not embedded and asks for, or downloads, a local copy
Does not invent content, numbers or dates that are not in the pasted report
